title: Jeet Analyzer Eternal Week 1
final_card: SELL DOES NOT NECESSARILY MEAN EXIT.

captions.text:
Jeet Analyzer started with one really simple question:
the jeet sold, but is he really out?

Most tools show that a wallet sold.
That does not tell you what happened to the position afterward.

So I built Jeet to reconstruct
the wallet's actual token lifecycle.

Here is a real Solana case
I anonymized for the demo.

Wallet A sold about 7.52 million tokens.
Its balance actually hit zero.

At that point, Jeet could defensibly
classify the wallet as VERIFIED OUT.
But that was not the end of the story.

Jeet continued following the lifecycle and found
Wallet A later bought back almost 5.97 million tokens.

The historical answer was true:
the wallet was out.

The current answer is different:
RE-ENTERED. NOT OUT.
That distinction is the point of Jeet Analyzer.

It checks inventory, transfers, re-entry, related-wallet evidence,
and coverage instead of treating one sell as the end.

It also refuses to make claims
the evidence cannot support.
In this case, common control is NOT PROVEN.

Downstream relationship coverage
is explicitly marked incomplete.

Real investigations exposed two generic classification and accounting defects.
Both were fixed and converted into regression tests.

The current build passes
155 Python tests and 16 frontend tests.

The original case used about 520 estimated provider credits.
This replay uses zero provider calls.

The jeet sold. He really was out.
Then he came back.
Jeet caught the whole story.
